removes.rationale: This week's only AAPL coverage is a speculative Bloomberg/Gurman leak about future satellite-feature roadmap items with no revenue or launch timeline attached -- a quiet, non-catalytic week that makes AAPL the weakest wave-linked slot to fund a clearer, earnings-backed rockets/spacecraft entry.

news_evidence.summary: Report describes Apple developing satellite-powered Maps, photo messaging, and third-party app support for iPhone -- roadmap speculation, no product or financial catalyst

rationale_overall: Filtered out heavy noise this week: Blue Origin/SpaceX/Starlink launch logistics (private, not investable), GoviEx Uranium (CVE-listed, thinly traded, not US-listed), Quantum Computing Inc (QUBT, down on no real catalyst), IBM's quantum 'breakthrough' headline (mega-cap, already priced, not an early-wave entry), Nvidia-backed Firmus funding (private company), Japan nuclear financing policy and Greenpeace uranium-to-Russia story (structural/geopolitical color, no specific US ticker), F-35/Saudi deal chatter and Russia-Ukraine drone barrage (geopolitical wave color, no named investable ticker), and general AI-adoption trend pieces (airlines, healthcare, EU AI Act) that named no tickers. The one genuine catalyst was Rocket Lab's record Q3 revenue beat, which finally gives the watchlist real exposure to the rockets & spacecraft wave; AAPL's only news this week was pure feature-roadmap speculation, making it the natural funding source for the swap while AI-wave holdings (GOOGL, NVDA) and the nuclear-wave holding (SMR) had either positive or neutral-but-thesis-intact news and were left untouched.
